title: Regional sharding & Zero-Trust gateway discovery - Redwood intro
summary: Discovery focused on private/VPC deployment for a latency-sensitive, region-gated ML feature. Main concerns: regional data residency, egress IPs, zero-trust interconnect, and whether Redwood Private can support sharded model endpoints across regions with consistent KV cache behavior and predictable failover.
next_steps: Alex to share VPC peering diagram and egress IP range spreadsheet
SE to run quick perf estimate for 2-region shard configuration
Customer to provide network contacts and a sample CIDR plan
Schedule technical deep-dive for week of 2026-03-08
action_items: Alex Moreno - Share VPC peering diagram + list of Redwood private endpoints - due 2026-03-08
Samira Patel - Prepare perf estimate for 2-region sharded inference (p99/latency and cost delta) - due 2026-03-09
Nina Zhao - Send current CIDR blocks and egress NAT gateway details - due 2026-03-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-03
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 mins
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SolEng), Nina Zhao (Infra Lead - StratusGrid), Carlos Mendez (Security Arch), Priya Rao (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
We talked about sharding Redwood Private across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 for a low-latency routing for their user base. Key asks: private endpoints (no public egress), region gating (data residency), and an explicit plan for egress IPs for customer firewalls. Customer emphasized zero-trust and KMS/HSM integration for keys.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros, I'll hand over to Samira to kick off the technical bits, but high level we want to understand your constraints around regions, networking, and trust requirements.

[00:28] Nina (Infra Lead): thanks alex. to be explicit, we are building a latencysensitive inference layer for our EU customers so we'll need eu-west and us-east shards. data residency is a hard requirement for certain records, also we have tight egress firewall rules so we need static IP ranges.

[00:46] Samira (Redwood SE): got it. when you say shards, do you mean independent model endpoints in each region with local KV cache, or a single global endpoint that routes? those have different tradeoffs on consistency vs hotspotting.

[01:10] Priya (Platform Eng): independent endpoints. we want traffic to terminate locally when possible and only tier to another region on miss, but we also care about warm starts and kv cash priming across regions. (laughs) sorry kv cash, kv cache.

[01:34] Jordan (SolEng): yeah so from Redwood Private, we support model pinning and routing policies - you can pin traffic by geo and set fallback to a secondary region. cache behavior is per-serving pool so cross-region cache priming will need an application-level strategy or a replication job.

[02:05] Carlos (Security): quick red flag for us: how do you handle key management? we need KMS/HSM integration, and audit trails accessible via our SIEM, plus SSO using SAML. also SOC2 reports would be required for procurement.

[02:32] Samira: absolutely, we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments and we can support BYOK via KMIP or cloud KMS depending on your environment. audit logs - we provide audit event streams and we can ship to your S3 or a secure syslog. we'll share our SOC2 report.

[03:10] Nina: do you have examples of how the private endpoints look? our security team is wary of any public egress by default.

[03:26] Alex: yes, for Private we give you VPC endpoints (PrivateLink-style) and optionally transit-gateway peering or direct-connect equivalent depending on cloud. we'll share a diagram.

[03:47] Priya: also want to call out regulatory constraints - for some EU customers we cannot egress tokens to us-east even for cache priming. can you enforce region gating per model?

[04:05] Samira: you can. routing policies can be configured on a per-route or per-model level to restrict to allowed regions; if a request would violate routing policy we can return a 403 or route to a compliant model variant.

[04:32] Carlos: about egress IPs - we need a fixed list for firewall allowlists. is that stable? what about shared hosted plans?

[04:45] Alex: with Dedicated and Private we can provide stable egress IP ranges; hosted has broader ranges and is less suitable for allowlisting. Private is what you'd want for strict firewalling.

[05:05] Nina: what about performance - if we shard models, how do we handle warmup so the p99 latency doesn't spike after failover?

[05:20] Samira: good question. we recommend proactive prewarming and using our prefetch endpoints to prime KV cache. also you can configure warm replicas. there is cost tradeoff - more warm replicas reduces cold-start p99, increases cost.

[05:48] Priya: approximate numbers, for our workload (short prompts, high QPS) what does a p99 look like in-region vs cross-region?

[06:02] Jordan: quick off-the-cuff: in-region p99 is sub-150ms for distilled models on modern infra, cross-region could add 80-200ms depending on RTT and routing; we'll run an estimate for your two-region config and share.

[06:28] Nina: can you document the failover behavior? for example if eu-west capacity hit, will traffic go to us-east automatically or pause? we need to avoid data residency breaches.

[06:46] Samira: you can set an explicit fallback policy - either deny, route to a regional-compliant stub, or route to another region but scrub request metadata. for strict customers we set to deny by default.

[07:12] Carlos: encryption in transit — do you do mTLS between our services and Redwood endpoints?

[07:22] Alex: yeah mTLS is supported, also SAML for user auth. for service-to-service we can provision client certs or integrate with your identity infra.

[07:38] Priya: any limitations around VPC size or CIDR overlap? we operate a large peered mesh and our CIDR ranges are somewhat unusual.

[07:52] Jordan: we generally recommend non-overlapping ranges; if overlap exists we can use NAT on our side or advertise via transit routing but it adds complexity. share your CIDRs and our network eng will sketch options.

[08:15] [minute marker jump, background noise] Nina: sorry, there's a ... airplane? not sure, (laughs).

[08:36] Alex: no problem. also wanted to surface one gotcha: if you use cross-region replication for KV priming, you'll need to consider consistency — some customers accept eventual consistency and write idempotent flows.

[09:05] Carlos: regarding compliance, will Redwood Private let us keep logs in-region only? we need logs to remain in eu-west for some customers.

[09:20] Samira: yes, data plane and logs can be configured per-region to be stored locally; control plane metadata may be routed through our central control plane unless you choose the on-prem variant. we can discuss a private control plane if required.

[09:48] Priya: what's the difference between transit-gateway peering and PrivateLink in your deployments? which is recommended?

[10:05] Jordan: PrivateLink (private endpoints) is simpler and more secure for single-region direct access — it avoids broad routing table exposure. Transit gateway is better for multi-VPC enterprise meshes and when you need high-throughput peering between many VNets. For your case, a mix: PrivateLink for app microservices and transit for central shared infra.

[10:36] Nina: what about IP whitelisting? how do we rotate those ranges? ops teams hate hunting for changes.

[10:49] Alex: we provide a stable egress IP set for Private, and we publish it to a short-lived CIDR list URL that you can poll; rotations are announced ahead of time and we coordinate with your network team.

[11:12] Carlos: ok procurement will want to see SOC2, encryption details, data flows and the contract clause about egress. can you share a redlined security pack?

[11:25] Alex: yes we'll share our security pack and SOC2, plus a sample data flow diagram.

[11:40] Priya: are there any known issues with region-gated routing and observability? we need traces and token-level cost breakdown per region.

[11:54] Samira: tracing works per-route; we can annotate spans with region. cost breakdown per-token per-region is available in the Console. there may be small mismatches in attribution during cross-region failover but we surface both source and execution region.

[12:18] Nina: curious re: rollout - if we want a canary in eu-west then expand, how do you do rollouts across Private?

[12:33] Jordan: we support A/B and canary rollouts by model version and by route; you can target by region and percentage, and set automatic rollback on error rate regression.

[12:56] Priya: networking nit: do you support AWS PrivateLink and Azure Private Endpoint both?

[13:08] Samira: yes both are supported, GCP Private Service Connect is supported as well. implementation details differ but conceptually the same.

[13:28] Carlos: competitor question: any customers who moved from Anthropic or OpenAI for similar needs? what's the deciding factor?

[13:40] Alex: we've seen migrations where customers needed predictable latency and private connectivity; they chose Redwood Private because of dedicated capacity guarantees and more deterministic egress IPs. we'll share a case study.

[14:00] Nina: ok logistics - who do we loop in on the network side for peering?

[14:08] Priya: I'll put in Navid (networks).

[14:20] Alex: great — next step we'll send a short packet: VPC peering diagram, egress IP spreadsheet, SOC2, and proposed dates for a deep technical session.

[14:38] Carlos: timeline - we are aiming for a pilot in Q2 with production early Q3, but procurement pace may push.

[14:50] Samira: that timeline sounds doable, we'll prioritize the perf estimate and network docs.

[15:05] Jordan: quick note on cost: sharding across regions increases base cost because of warm replicas; cross-region requests also add egress charges if you have replication turned on. we'll model that in the perf estimate.

[15:28] Nina: ok good to know.

[15:40] [crosstalk briefly] Priya: one more question: for BYOK, how do key rotations work? can we rotate without downtime?

[15:55] Samira: yes rotating keys is designed to be rolling; you can configure dual keys during rotation windows to avoid service impact. we'll send key rotation docs.

[16:10] Alex: we'll summarize and send — anything else?

[16:20] Nina: nothing from infra besides the CIDR list; we'll send that.

[16:28] Carlos: security will review the pack.

[16:35] Alex: great. recap of action items: (1) Alex share network & security pack; (2) Samira share perf estimate for two-region shard; (3) Nina share CIDR and ops contact. schedule deep-dive for week of Mar 8.

[16:55] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps (kv cash), some timestamps approximate, minor crosstalk. Links referenced: "Redwood security pack (link to drive)"; "egress-ip spreadsheet (link)" — will be attached in follow-up email.
